Safeguards — code history and updates

How SATOM protects its own repository history and how code and dependency updates are snapshotted, smoke-tested, health-checked and rolled back automatically.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
📍 WhereSettings → Software update; Admin → System backup (repository bundles)
On this page
  • Repository history
  • Code and dependency updates
  • Related alerts

Repository history#

The repository carries the application code. Device configuration is not kept in git: since 2026-08-05 it lives in a local, content-addressed history that is replicated to the standby and carried in every backup bundle (see Source of truth).

The git remote is a distribution point, not a place of custody — and the dangerous moment is not a remote outage, it is the moment the remote comes back and an update resets the checkout.

Guard What it prevents
Commit preservation before a hard reset Losing commits that exist only on this node. Before an update resets the checkout, local commits are parked on permanent refs/backup/* references, a dirty working tree included. If they cannot be parked, the update aborts — a deferred update beats silent history loss.
Unpushed-commit alert A push failing quietly for days. The signal is the age of the oldest unpushed commit, not the count, because one commit stuck for three days is worse than twenty from the last hour.
Repository bundles Total loss. One verifiable, clonable file holds the entire history and every reference — kept on the node, mirrored to the standby, pushed to an external backup server in a different failure domain, and downloadable from the UI.
Bundle deletes are primary-only Deleting a bundle on the standby, where the next data sync would restore it and make the UI look broken.
Insert-only catalog seeds A deploy overwriting endpoint or provider rows that an operator corrected. When a vendor moves a REST path, the fix stays a row edit, not a release.

💡Tip — Bundles can be verified offline

git bundle verify proves a bundle's integrity, git clone <bundle> rebuilds the whole repository, and a checksum sidecar file lets you trust a copy before you use it. No server, no daemon and no embedded credentials are needed. See System backup.

Code and dependency updates#

The web process never changes the installation itself. It writes a request; a privileged runner picks the request up and does the work. The update path therefore cannot be reached by whatever reaches the web application (see Privilege boundary and operator console).

Every update — code or dependency — follows the same sequence:

  1. 1SnapshotThe current revision or installed package version is recorded
  2. 2ApplyThe code is updated or the pinned version is installed
  3. 3Smoke testThe application must still import
  4. 4Health checkThe service is restarted, then checked over real HTTP
  5. 5RevertAny failure restores the snapshot
Guard What it prevents
Snapshot, smoke test, health check, automatic revert A half-applied update. If the new code or library fails to import or the restarted service fails its health check, the recorded revision or version is restored and re-verified.
Curated-only dependency upgrades Remote code execution as the service account. The allowlist is the application's own library inventory; a request is validated when it is queued and again inside the privileged runner, with name and version pattern checks. There is deliberately no "install any package" path from the browser.
Recorded previous version per node A rollback that requires guesswork. The previous version is recorded on each node before the change, so rollback is one click.
Per-node scope, stated on the card Expecting a library change to reach both nodes. The virtual environment is not replicated, so the card names the node it will affect.
Dependency pin committed from the primary only The next code update undoing a library upgrade. The pin is committed by the single git writer (the primary), so later updates carry it.

💡Tip

To run an update or a library upgrade, see Software update. For air-gapped nodes, see Offline updates.

Related alerts#

The Unpushed commits, Behind / diverged and Backup missing / stale / error signals in the alert catalog are the alerting half of these guards.
